name: Security & DevSecOps
purpose: Coverage gap content. No existing learner covers security. Should trigger create signal via queries.
items: Ran SAST scan on the monorepo — found 14 SQL injection risks in the legacy query builder. All raw string concatenation. Migrating to parameterized queries this sprint.
Implemented RBAC with fine-grained permissions. Moved from 3 roles (admin/editor/viewer) to attribute-based access. Policy engine evaluates at request time.
Container image scanning in CI caught a critical CVE in our base Node image. Alpine 3.18 has an OpenSSL vulnerability. Pinned to 3.19.1.
Secrets rotation: moved all API keys from .env files to HashiCorp Vault. Auto-rotation every 30 days. Dynamic database credentials per service instance.
OAuth2 flow had a redirect_uri validation bypass. Attacker could use open redirect on our domain to steal auth codes. Added strict allowlist for redirect URIs.
Implemented CSP headers across all frontend apps. Blocked inline scripts, restricted connect-src to our API domains. XSS reports dropped to zero.
Dependency supply chain attack: compromised npm package published under typosquatted name. Our lockfile integrity check caught the hash mismatch before install.
API rate limiting redesigned: per-user token bucket with sliding window. 100 req/min for authenticated, 20 for anon. Redis-backed with Lua atomicity.
Penetration test results: 2 critical, 5 high, 12 medium findings. Criticals were SSRF via webhook URL and JWT algorithm confusion (none→HS256 bypass).
Implemented audit logging for all admin actions. Every mutation logged with actor, action, target, timestamp, IP, and request context. Immutable append-only store.
Moved from symmetric JWT (HS256) to asymmetric (RS256). Public key distributed to all services for verification. Private key stays in auth service only.
DAST pipeline stage runs OWASP ZAP against staging after every deploy. Found reflected XSS in search parameter that our unit tests missed.
Implemented subresource integrity (SRI) for all CDN-loaded scripts. SHA-384 hashes verified by browser. Prevents CDN compromise from injecting malicious code.
Database encryption at rest enabled. AES-256 with AWS KMS managed keys. Key rotation quarterly. Performance impact negligible — <2% overhead on reads.
Security training for dev team: ran a phishing simulation. 30% clicked the link. Now doing monthly security awareness sessions and mandatory MFA everywhere.
Implemented certificate pinning for mobile apps. Prevents MITM attacks even with compromised CAs. Pin backup certificates for rotation without app update.
Web Application Firewall rules updated: blocking known attack patterns, rate limiting by geo, bot detection via JavaScript challenges. False positive rate <0.1%.
Threat modeling session for the payment flow. Used STRIDE methodology. Identified 8 threats, 3 need immediate mitigation: replay attacks, privilege escalation, data leakage.
Implemented network segmentation: public-facing services in DMZ, databases in private subnet, admin tools in separate VPC. Inter-VPC traffic through managed NAT.
Security incident response plan documented: detection → containment → eradication → recovery → lessons learned. Runbook for top 5 incident types. On-call rotation established.
CORS configuration was too permissive — Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on authenticated endpoints. Tightened to explicit origin allowlist with credential support.
Implemented input validation layer: all API inputs pass through Zod schemas before reaching business logic. Rejected 12% of requests last week — mostly malformed JSON.
Vulnerability disclosure program launched: responsible disclosure policy, security.txt file, PGP-signed acknowledgments. First valid report within 48 hours.
Session management overhaul: server-side sessions with Redis store, 15-minute sliding expiry, absolute 8-hour limit, session binding to IP/UA fingerprint.
Code signing for all release artifacts. GPG-signed commits required for main branch. CI verifies signatures before building. Tamper-evident release pipeline.
Implemented mutual TLS between microservices. Each service has its own certificate from internal CA. Zero-trust networking — no implicit trust based on network position.
SQL injection in legacy admin panel: parameter was double-encoded, bypassing our WAF rules. Fixed the WAF regex and migrated the endpoint to parameterized queries.
Privacy impact assessment for new analytics feature. GDPR Article 35 DPIA completed. Pseudonymization of user IDs, 90-day retention, purpose limitation documented.
Implemented secure file upload: virus scanning with ClamAV, content-type validation (magic bytes, not just extension), size limits, sandboxed processing.
Red team exercise: internal team attempted lateral movement from compromised dev workstation. Reached staging DB in 3 hours. Gaps: shared SSH keys, flat network.
